question.text: A screw gauge with a pitch of <math><mn>0.5 </mn><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mtext>mm</mtext><mtext></mtext></math> and a circular scale with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn></math> divisions is used to measure the thickness of a thin sheet of aluminum. Before starting the measurement, it is found that when the two jaws of the screw gauge are brought in contact, the <math><msup><mrow><mn>45</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi></math> division coincides with the main scale line and that the zero of the main scale is barely visible. What is the thickness (in <math><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>) of the sheet if the main scale reading is <math><mn>0.5 </mn><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mtext>mm</mtext></math> and the <math><msup><mrow><mn>30</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi></math> division coincides with the main scale line?

solution.text:
Least count, LC=0.550=0.01 mm

Zero error, ZE=50-45×0.01=-0.05 mm

Main Scale Reading MSR=0.5 mm
Thickness, t=0.5 mm +30×0.01 mm - -0.05 mm

t=0.85 mm
